summary: Say what --iter actually filters on - every state the bill has traversed, not its current one - and declare the source index's lag on recent bills.
reason: The flag read "Stato dell'iter", which promises the current state. The ITERST field indexes the whole history: bill 779, presented in 2024, comes back from --iter "Assegnato" --anno 2024 while being much further along. A list that looks like today's snapshot and is not is the worst false signal for anyone building on it. The same flag was documented nowhere but --help. Measured alongside: the source's index lags on recent bills - bill 1196, assigned on 2026-08-05, was still absent from --iter "Assegnato" --anno 2026 on 2026-09-06 - so an undercount can read as an absence of acts.
validated_outcome: ddl cerca --help states the traversed-state semantics, names ddl iter for the current state of one act, and carries the measured index lag; SKILL.md and README document the flag, which they did not mention at all. The stale "Stato dell'iter (atto/storico)" copy in the MCP tool schema and in tools-manifest.json is updated too, so an agent reading the schema gets the same semantics as a human reading --help.
